summary: A 60-foot forest fire tower raised on Muirkirk Road in 1926 was moved to Burtonsville in 1932 and demolished in 2014; the association lists it as gone.

facts.design: 60-foot forest fire lookout tower, as first erected in 1926
facts.status_note: Demolished in 2014. A scrambled passage in the DocsLib copy may say that no physical remains are left at the site, but it does not say which tower it describes.
facts.agency: Maryland Department of Forestry (erected the tower in 1926)

events.note: Erected at 7813 Muirkirk Road as a 60-foot forest fire lookout by the Department of Forestry
Dismantled and re-assembled along Columbia Pike (US Route 29) in Burtonsville
Demolished because of its deteriorated condition and the lack of a remaining communications need

evidence.quote: The project was initiated because the University owned Burtonsville Fire Tower, which was built in 1926, but was later moved to a site along Columbia Pike (US Route 29), was proposed to be demolished.

notes_for_editor: Source 3 is a copy with its table and narrative interleaved by OCR, so quotes were chosen only where the wording reads in one piece. The 1926 erection at Muirkirk Road and the 1932 move rest on that copy alone; source 1 confirms the Columbia Pike move and the 1926 build year, but not the Muirkirk location or the 1932 date. The copy's table also lists the Muirkirk tower (1926, 60 ft) as relocated to #19 Burtonsville, which supports the move. The 1932 date sits in the copy beside the re-assembly text, so the story dates only the move, not the dismantling. This is the same structure as the Muirkirk record (us-md-muirkirk): its research file calls the 1932 move unconfirmed, and this copy supports it, so that file can be updated. A 2017 University of Maryland Board of Regents item (usmd.edu PDF) about conveying the Burtonsville Fire Tower property to Montgomery County did not fetch (certificate error) and is not cited; worth retrying. The copy's table gives 100 feet for the Burtonsville tower against 60 feet in the 1926 narrative; the record uses 60 feet only for the 1926 erection, as the narrative states, and does not use the table figure. No staffing or fire evidence was found. Searches used: 2 (cap 2). Pages read: 4, including one that failed. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the closing line now reports the scrambled remains passage instead of saying no source describes remains.
